key_insight: Turbulence-driven ice-crystal orientation changes scattering and can bias ice-water-content retrievals that assume perfectly horizontal alignment.
engineering_relevance: Orientation-aware scattering models can improve interpretation of polarimetric radar, lidar and submillimeter measurements of ice clouds.
method: Model overdamped spheroid orientations with settling torque, turbulent gradients, rotational diffusion and intermittency.
Average Rayleigh, Rayleigh–Gans, T-matrix and specular scattering over the orientation distribution.
Link orientation moments to scattering observables and retrieval biases.
evidence_signal: For single-size populations of the studied shapes, combining specific differential phase with differential reflectivity limits retrieval bias to 25%; exploratory EarthCARE lidar analysis finds a compatible signature most frequent near −11 °C.
watch_item: The 25% bias bound can fail for size distributions spanning the alignment transition, and degree-scale tilt widths require crystals near or beyond the model’s validity range.
paper_title: Scattering by Small Ice Crystals in Turbulence: From Orientation Statistics to Retrieval Biases
